clue.text: Regular event somehow represented in mono?

parts.note: read the other way round, a recast version of the word moon gives these clue words: the fresh word signals rearrangement and the letters of moon rearranged spell mono

explanation.surface: Something recurring has been rearranged and reproduced in mono rather than stereo.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, means MOON made new, i.e. rearranged, which gives 'mono'; 'somehow represented' describes that rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the moon is unlit recurs about every 29.5 days, so it is a regular event.

clue.text: Comprehensive directions to thoroughfare and where you'll find copies of the TLS?

definitions.text: where you'll find copies of the TLS

parts.note: all four compass points, north, east, west and south, abbreviated N, E, W, S
ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Someone gives full directions to the street where the literary weekly is sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive directions' means all four compass points, N, E, W and S, in an order that happens to spell a real word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk selling papers and magazines is where a reader would buy a weekly review.

clue.text: One extricating an American actor

definitions.meaning: someone who winkles something out, prising it loose as one picks a shellfish from its shell
Henry ..., the American actor who played the Fonz in Happy Days

explanation.surface: Someone is getting a Hollywood star out of a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To winkle out is to extract with effort, so the agent noun is an extractor; it is also the surname of a US actor.

clue.text: I'd seen a small company cast as nymphs here

indicators.note: to cast is to mould into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: CO is the short form of company

explanation.surface: Someone saw a modest theatre troupe cast in the roles of nymphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as theatrical casting but signals rearranging the letters of I'D SEEN A plus CO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the daughters of Oceanus were sea nymphs.

clue.text: Exercise taken by Fleming's doctor? Negative

indicators.note: the exercise is taken on by the doctor, so it comes after the doctor's name

parts.note: Dr No is the villain of Ian Fleming's Bond novel
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Asked whether Ian Fleming's doctor does any exercise, the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleming's doctor' is Dr No, from Ian Fleming's James Bond novel, giving NO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal way of saying no, a negative reply.

clue.text: Suppose rum's replacing a bit of usquebaugh — that's the spirit!

indicators.note: the strange word is put in where the named letter stood, replacing it

parts.note: to suppose is to guess

indicators.note: a bit of the word usquebaugh is just its opening letter

parts.note: rum means odd or strange; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A drinker supposes rum has taken the place of a drop of whisky, and approves.
explanation.walkthrough: Usquebaugh is Gaelic-derived for whisky, but only its first letter, U, is wanted: in GUESS, ODD replaces that U.
explanation.definitionFit: A goddess is a divine being, a spirit in the sense of a supernatural presence.

clue.text: Whisky astronaut, we hear, and others blanded

indicators.note: says the astronaut's surname is taken by its sound, losing one N

parts.note: John Glenn, the American astronaut, first American to orbit the Earth

indicators.note: a misprint for blended; blending mixes the letters of the word others

explanation.surface: A whisky is advertised with a pun on an astronaut's name and a mix of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blanded' is the setter's or printer's slip for 'blended', the anagram signal; GLEN sounds like Glenn.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenrothes is a Speyside single malt Scotch, a named whisky.

clue.text: A Mitford girl, one to worship!

definitions.meaning: ... Mitford, one of the famous Mitford sisters
the Roman goddess of hunting and the moon, an object of worship

explanation.surface: One of the Mitford sisters is declared worthy of adoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mitfords were six English sisters of the 1920s and 30s, famous socialites and writers.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Mitford sister and to a Roman goddess.

clue.text: Involves absence of resistance in internal organs

indicators.note: the absence of something means it is taken away from the rest

parts.note: entrails are the guts, internal organs
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A medical note says a condition involves organs offering no resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require or involve it as a consequence.

clue.text: One of a group Odysseus at last destroyed in heartless rage

indicators.note: only the final letter of the hero's name is taken, at the very end
destroyed means broken up, so these letters are reassembled
heartless removes the middle of the word rage, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Odysseus finally wipes out one of a band of enemies in a merciless fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' looks like it describes what Odysseus did, but it is the anagram signal. 'heartless rage' leaves the first and last letters of rage, RE, which are mixed with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirens were a group of sea creatures whose song lured sailors to wreck; Odysseus resisted them.

clue.text: "Let the galled jade -, our withers are unwrung" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "Let the galled jade -, our withers are unwrung" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "Let the galled jade -, our withers are unwrung" (Hamlet)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from Hamlet's line during the play scene: a sore horse may flinch, but the speaker is unhurt

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says this to Claudius during the play: let the guilty party flinch, the innocent feel nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A galled horse flinches from pain, which is what the missing verb describes.

clue.text: Inferior versifier providing sample of taleteller's works

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, teller of tales of mystery, standing for his writings
a taster is a small sample

explanation.surface: Someone is offering a sample of a storyteller's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the pieces: a taster OF Poe, with POE written first.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of trivial or bad verse, a poor poet.

clue.text: Personification of a satellite seen with luminance and eccentricity varying

indicators.note: varying means changing, so these letters change order

parts.note: L is the symbol for luminance
e is the symbol for orbital eccentricity

explanation.surface: An astronomer describes a satellite observed with brightness and orbit changing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the goddess who embodies the Moon, Earth's satellite.

clue.text: Wesker paid outrageously for a pianist

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The playwright Arnold Wesker paid a scandalous fee to hire a pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Wesker was an English playwright; his name plus PAID is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignacy Jan Paderewski was a celebrated Polish concert pianist who became prime minister.

clue.text: Communist following one I broadcast

indicators.note: the communist follows, so it comes after the other letters

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing
red is a common name for a communist

explanation.surface: Someone admits to broadcasting after a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Aired means put out on radio or television, the past tense sense of broadcast.

clue.text: Irate with endless miasm perhaps; an extract of this will help

definitions.text: an extract of this will help

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters may be arranged otherwise
endless means the word miasm loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone angry with a lingering foul vapour is told a herbal extract will help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims MIASM to MIAS; 'perhaps' rearranges IRATE with MIAS. Miasm is a noxious vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood and mugwort belong to this plant genus, whose extracts are used medicinally, as against malaria.

clue.text: 1A to design drug that will transport you

parts.note: the 1 across answer means the moon made new, i.e. its letters rearranged, giving mono
a plan is a design
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A drug is designed to carry you away to a new state of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference to 1 across works through that clue's trick: a rearranged moon is MONO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft with one pair of wings carries passengers through the air.

clue.text: With hairstyle we hear tied about Allen's was mighty

indicators.note: says the hairstyle word is taken by its sound and spelt differently

parts.note: an afro is a bushy rounded hairstyle

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the word tied are moved around

explanation.surface: A hairstyle is tied up, in a description of Woody Allen's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Woody Allen's 1995 film is titled Mighty Aphrodite; APHRO sounds like AFRO, and 'about' rearranges TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of love names the film Woody Allen called mighty.

clue.text: Like a conversion achieved by sword?

definitions.meaning: St Paul's sudden conversion on the road to Damascus, hence any sudden change of heart
inlaid or watered like a Damascus blade, decorated metalwork

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a conversion was gained at sword-point.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both a sudden revelation and the patterned steel of Damascus swords.

clue.text: 1940s housewife as diminutive TV detective briefly

parts.note: mini means small, diminutive

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the detective's name

parts.note: DCI Vera Stanhope, title character of the ITV crime drama Vera

explanation.surface: A wartime housewife is likened to a tiny television detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera is a British TV crime series about a Northumbrian detective; trimmed it gives VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Miniver, the 1942 film, follows an English housewife in the Second World War.

clue.text: Direction travelled by Fitzgerald's alcoholic composer?

definitions.meaning: Abe ..., the hard-drinking composer in F Scott Fitzgerald's Tender Is the Night

explanation.surface: The way an alcoholic composer in a Fitzgerald novel went.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a compass point and the surname of a character in Fitzgerald's novel.

clue.text: Trusting priest to get consumed by tirade

indicators.note: being consumed by means being swallowed inside something

parts.note: a rant is a tirade
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A trusting cleric is swallowed up by an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel, is the usual crossword priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant means dependent, putting trust in someone.

clue.text: Mackenzie's Oxford steward or Jennings' school-friend

definitions.meaning: the college scout in Compton Mackenzie's novel Sinister Street
Darbishire's rival and Jennings's classmate in Anthony Buckeridge's school stories

explanation.surface: Two characters from English fiction, a college servant and a schoolboy.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to a servant in Mackenzie's Oxford novel and a boy in the Jennings books.

clue.text: Poison coven omitted in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A witch's poison has been left out by the coven.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom is the toxin of snakes and spiders, a poison.

clue.text: Bear initially taking a brief glance at Mowgli

definitions.text: Bear initially taking a brief glance at Mowgli

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word bear
brief cuts the last letter off the word for a glance

parts.note: a look is a glance

explanation.surface: A bear first has a quick look at the jungle boy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's Jungle Book the bear who teaches Mowgli is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The bear in The Jungle Book is the one who looks after Mowgli.

clue.text: "The words of Mercury are harsh after the songs of —" (Love's Labours Lost)

definitions.text: "The words of Mercury are harsh after the songs of —" (Love's Labours Lost)

parts.words: "The words of Mercury are harsh after the songs of —" (Love's Labours Lost)
parts.note: a gap-fill quotation from the closing line of Shakespeare's comedy, contrasting the messenger god with the god of music

explanation.walkthrough: The play ends with this line, naming the god of music and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of music and song fits the contrast with harsh words of the messenger god.

clue.text: One sister … of Osiris

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The clue names a sister of the Egyptian god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian goddess was both sister and wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Writers composing violent scenarios on vacation

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters are assembled anew
on vacation means the word is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Authors are drafting brutal plots while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties SCENARIOS to SS, which joins VIOLENT for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelists are authors of long fiction, so they are writers.

clue.text: In Cremona matins might be accompanied by his instruments

definitions.text: In Cremona matins might be accompanied by his instruments

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Morning prayers in Cremona might be played on a local violin maker's instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amati family were violin makers of Cremona, Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Amati and his family made violins in Cremona, so church music there might be played on theirs.

clue.text: Inventor to learn hastily over on island

indicators.note: over says the swotting word is turned back to front

parts.note: to cram is to learn quickly before an exam

explanation.surface: An inventor goes over his notes in a hurry while on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as 'about' in the surface, but it signals reading the swotting word backwards, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi developed radio telegraphy, a celebrated inventor.

clue.text: Quietly surrounded by group dealing with fictional terrorists

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside another word

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning, dealing with

explanation.surface: A group is quietly surrounded while handling a band of terrorists in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The criminal organisation fighting James Bond is the fictional terrorist group.
explanation.definitionFit: SPECTRE is the villainous organisation in Ian Fleming's Bond novels.
